text: Driving a small car is much more _____ than driving a large one.
note: Economical = cheap to use, not wasteful. Economic = about the economy (an economic crisis). Economics is the subject; the economy is a country's money system.

text: The _____ reason for the delay was the bad weather.
note: Principal (adjective) = main. A principle is a rule or belief (a matter of principle). Principally is an adverb: it is mainly due to the weather.

text: It would be more _____ to leave early and avoid the traffic.
note: Sensible = showing good judgement. Sensitive = easily affected or upset. (In Spanish, sensible means sensitive: a false friend.)

text: Be careful what you say about her job. She is very _____ about it.
note: Sensitive about something = easily upset by it. Sensible = showing good judgement.

text: Are you trying to _____ that I made a mistake?
note: The speaker implies (suggests without saying). The listener infers (works out). Implicate = show that someone is involved in a crime.

text: From the tone of her voice, I _____ that she was not happy.
note: Infer = work out a meaning from clues. The speaker implies or hints; the listener infers.

text: I can _____ you that the food is perfectly safe to eat.
note: Assure someone that = promise, to make them feel certain. Ensure = make certain that. Insure = buy insurance.

text: Please _____ that all the windows are closed before you leave.
note: Ensure that = make sure. Assure and reassure need a person after them (assure you); insure is about insurance.

text: Could you _____ me your pen for a moment?
note: You lend something to someone, and they borrow it from you. Lend = give for a time.

text: Can I _____ your dictionary until tomorrow?
note: Borrow = take something from someone for a time. You lend; the other person borrows.

text: Prices are expected to _____ again next month.
note: Rise has no object: prices rise (rose, risen). Raise needs an object: raise prices.

text: The government plans to _____ taxes next year.
note: Raise + object (raise taxes, raise a question). Rise has no object: taxes rise.

text: Don't _____ your keys again!
note: Lose /luːz/ is the verb (lose, lost, lost). Loose /luːs/ means not tight. A loss is the noun.

text: These trousers are too _____ . Do you have a smaller size?
note: Loose = not tight. Lose is the verb. Lax = not strict (lax security), not used for clothes.

text: For _____ information, please visit our website.
note: Further = more, additional. Farther is only about distance (a farther walk), and even then further is common.

text: _____ being cheap, the hotel is in a wonderful location.
note: Besides = in addition to. Beside = next to (beside the sea).

text: My brother is three years _____ than me.
note: Older than is the normal comparison. Elder is used before a noun (my elder sister) and never with "than".

text: We had a lot of _____ at the beach yesterday.
note: Fun is a noun: have fun. Funny is an adjective meaning amusing (a funny story) or strange.

text: It was a _____ moment when the two countries signed the peace treaty.
note: Historic = important in history. Historical = connected with the past (a historical novel).

text: She _____ me that she was leaving the company.
note: Tell someone (that). Say that, without the person: she said that she was leaving.

text: Everyone _____ Tom came to the party.
note: Except = not including. Accept means "take what is offered", and expect means "think that something will happen".

text: She gave me some very good _____ about where to stay.
note: Advice is the noun (and has no plural); advise is the verb: I advise you to book early.

text: I'd _____ you to see a doctor about that cough.
note: Advise is the verb (rhymes with "size"); advice is the noun (rhymes with "ice").

text: The loud music didn't _____ my sleep at all.
note: Affect (verb) = have an influence on. Effect is usually a noun: the effect of the music.

text: Take a deep _____ and try to relax.
note: Breath (noun, short vowel) = the air you take in. Breathe (verb, long vowel) = to take air in and out.

text: She _____ the red dress yesterday, but today she wants the blue one.
note: Chose is the past of choose. Chosen is the past participle (has chosen), and choice is the noun.

text: She was wearing her best _____ for the wedding.
note: Clothes = things you wear. Cloths are pieces of material for cleaning, and close means "near" or "shut".

text: He paid me a lovely _____ about my new haircut.
note: A compliment = a kind remark. A complement is something that completes another thing.

text: We had chocolate cake for _____.
note: Dessert (two s) = the sweet course at the end of a meal. A desert is a dry, sandy place.

text: Engineers have designed a new _____ for measuring heart rate.
note: A device (noun, ends in -ice) = a machine or tool. To devise (verb, ends in -ise) = to plan or invent.

text: The dog wagged _____ tail happily.
note: Its (no apostrophe) = belonging to it. It's = it is or it has.

text: Please _____ the book on the table when you have finished.
note: Lay = put something down (it takes an object). Lie = rest flat (no object). Laid is the past of lay.

text: She walked _____ the bank without looking at it.
note: Past (preposition) = going by. Passed is the past tense of the verb pass: she passed the bank.

text: Would you like another _____ of cake?
note: A piece = a part of something. Peace = calm, no war.

text: It was _____ a long journey, but we enjoyed it.
note: Quite = fairly, rather. Quiet = making little noise.

text: The car was _____ at the traffic lights.
note: Stationary = not moving. Stationery = paper, pens and other writing materials.

text: She is much taller _____ her brother.
note: Than is used to compare things. Then refers to time: first we ate, then we left.

text: _____ going to be late because of the traffic.
note: They're = they are. Their = belonging to them. There = in that place.

text: He _____ the ball over the fence and into the garden.
note: Threw is the past of throw. Through is a preposition: through the door.

text: I don't know _____ I should accept the job.
note: Whether introduces a choice (whether or not). Weather is about rain, sun and wind.

text: _____ coat is this? It was left on the sofa.
note: Whose asks who something belongs to. Who's = who is or who has.

text: _____ very kind to help me with my bags.
note: You're = you are. Your = belonging to you.

text: The old factory _____ will soon be turned into a park.
note: A site = a place where something is or will be. Sight = the ability to see. To cite = to quote.

text: I prefer the _____ of the two options, because it is cheaper.
note: The latter = the second of two things just mentioned. Later means "after", and latest means "most recent".

text: The thieves _____ jewellery worth £5,000 from the house.
note: You steal things, but you rob or burgle a place or a person.

text: My uncle _____ me to swim when I was six.
note: Teach (taught) = give someone knowledge. Learn = receive it.

text: Please _____ me to post the letter when we leave.
note: Remind someone to do something. Remember is what you do yourself.

text: I can't _____ you; the music is too loud.
note: Hear = receive sound without trying. Listen needs "to" before the person, and it means paying attention on purpose.

text: I met her three years _____ at a conference.
note: Ago counts back from now (three years ago). Before counts back from a time in the past.

text: He lives _____ in a small house at the end of the road.
note: Alone = without other people. Lonely = unhappy because you are alone, and it is an adjective, so it can't describe how he lives.

text: I like all sports, _____ tennis.
note: Especially = above all. Specially = for a particular purpose: a cake made specially for her.

text: I _____ missed the last train.
note: Nearly = almost. Near is about distance.

text: The door was _____ open, so we walked straight in.
note: Wide (adverb) = fully. Widely means "in many places" or "by many people": a widely known fact.

text: The plane flew _____ above the clouds.
note: High (adverb) = at a great height. Highly = very (highly successful).

text: She was _____ upset by the news of the accident.
note: Deeply = very much, with strong feeling. Deep (adverb) is for position: deep in the forest.

text: _____ we should go home and try again tomorrow.
note: Maybe = perhaps (one word, an adverb). May be (two words) = a verb phrase: it may be true.

text: I fell _____ asleep during the long film.
note: Fall fast asleep = fall into a deep sleep. Fast is both the adjective and the adverb; there is no "fastly".

text: His grandfather _____ last year at the age of ninety.
note: Died is the past tense of the verb die. Dead is an adjective: he is dead. Death is the noun.

text: Our _____ was delayed by two hours because of fog.
note: A flight = a journey by plane. Flying is the activity, and fly is the verb.

text: She _____ a new coat in the sales yesterday.
note: Bought is the past of buy. Brought is the past of bring.

text: The name of the song _____ me, but I can almost remember it.
note: Elude = escape from, or not be remembered. Allude to = mention indirectly. Elicit = get a response.

text: The police failed to _____ any useful information from the witness.
note: Elicit = get a reaction or information from someone. Illicit (adjective) = illegal.

text: Heavy snow is _____ , so the airport may have to close.
note: Imminent = about to happen. Eminent = famous and respected (an eminent scientist).

text: She came up with an _____ solution to the problem.
note: Ingenious = clever and original. Ingenuous = innocent and trusting. Indigenous = native to a place.

text: The witness gave a clear and _____ account of what happened.
note: Credible = believable. Credulous = too ready to believe. Creditable = good enough to be praised.

text: Only a _____ person would believe such a story.
note: Credulous = believing too easily. A story is credible (believable); a person is credulous.

text: The local _____ has decided to build a new library.
note: A council is a group that governs or advises. Counsel = advice (or a lawyer). A consul is a diplomat.

text: Her calm words helped to _____ the tense situation.
note: Defuse = make less dangerous or tense (remove the fuse from a bomb). Diffuse = spread out.

text: A new car will _____ in value by about 20 per cent in its first year.
note: Depreciate = lose value. Deprecate = express disapproval of. Appreciate can mean gain value.

text: Drivers who _____ the speed limit risk heavy fines.
note: Flout a rule or law = openly ignore it. Flaunt = show off.

text: She likes to _____ her wealth by wearing expensive jewellery.
note: Flaunt = show off proudly. Flout = openly ignore a rule.

text: Many people were _____ for their political beliefs.
note: Persecute = treat someone cruelly, usually for their beliefs. Prosecute = take legal action against.

text: Anyone caught dumping rubbish here will be _____ .
note: Prosecute = take to court. Persecute = treat cruelly.

text: The mirrors on the walls create an _____ of space.
note: Illusion = something that seems real but isn't. Allusion = an indirect reference. Delusion = a false belief.

text: Please be _____ about what you saw. It is confidential.
note: Discreet = careful not to say or do anything embarrassing or secret. Discrete = separate.

text: A short speech will _____ the dinner.
note: Precede = come before. Proceed = continue, go ahead. (The noun is precedent.)

text: The building was _____ a school but is now a hotel.
note: Formerly = in the past. Formally = in an official or polite way.

text: Anna and Tom are 25 and 30, _____ .
note: Respectively = in the order mentioned. Respectfully = in a polite, respectful way.

text: The journey along the _____ mountain road took six hours.
note: Tortuous = full of twists and turns. Torturous = very painful, like torture. Many people mix them up.

text: There is no _____ route; the bridge is the only way across.
note: Alternative = another possible choice. Alternate = every second one (on alternate days) or take turns.

text: He is not _____ to taking risks when the rewards are high.
note: Averse (to) = strongly disliking. Adverse = unfavourable (adverse weather).

text: The match was cancelled because of _____ weather conditions.
note: Adverse = bad and harmful. Averse (to) describes people who dislike something.

text: I will _____ you of any change in the schedule as soon as I know.
note: Apprise someone of something = tell them about it. Appraise = judge the value or quality of.

text: The king gave his royal _____ to the new law.
note: Assent = official agreement. An ascent is a climb up.

text: A _____ festival is held every two years, and the next one is in 2028.
note: Biennial = every two years. Biannual = twice a year.

text: The full cost of the repairs will be _____ by the taxpayer.
note: Borne is the past participle of bear in the sense of "carry or pay". Born is used for birth: she was born in 1990.

text: The minister was publicly _____ for his offensive remarks.
note: Censure = criticise strongly. Censor = remove parts of a book, film or news.

text: Scientists are studying _____ changes over the last century.
note: Climatic = about the climate. Climactic = forming the most exciting point of a story.

text: After years of success, the company had become _____ and stopped innovating.
note: Complacent = too satisfied with how things are. Complaisant means "willing to please others".

text: She managed to _____ a clever plan to escape.
note: Devise (verb) = invent or plan. A device (noun) is a machine or tool.

text: The police used tear gas to _____ the crowd.
note: Disperse = make a group go away in different directions. Disburse = pay out money, and dispel = make a feeling or belief disappear.

text: A thick mist began to _____ the valley.
note: Envelop (verb, no final e) = cover or surround completely. An envelope holds a letter.

text: The police discovered a _____ scene at the old farmhouse.
note: Grisly = causing horror and disgust. A grizzly is a type of bear.

text: She stared at him in _____ disbelief.
note: Incredulous = unwilling to believe. Incredible describes something hard to believe.

text: It was a _____ decision to sell the shares before the market fell.
note: Judicious = showing good judgement. Judicial = about courts of law.

text: He had a thick, _____ beard that reached his chest.
note: Luxuriant = growing thickly and healthily (hair, plants). Luxurious means expensive and comfortable, and luxury is the noun.

text: These factors _____ against the success of the plan.
note: Militate against something = make it less likely. Mitigate = make less serious.

text: Staff _____ has been very low since the announcement of job cuts.
note: Morale = the confidence and enthusiasm of a group. A moral is a lesson; morals are principles of right and wrong.

text: Please contact the _____ department if you have a question about your contract.
note: Personnel = the people who work for an organisation. Personal = private.

text: _____ buyers should contact the estate agent for a viewing.
note: Prospective = likely to become (a prospective buyer). Perspective = a way of seeing things, and respective means "belonging to each one".

text: The child gave a _____ cry that made everyone turn round.
note: Plaintive = sounding sad. A plaintiff is a person who starts a legal case.

text: What is the _____ behind this decision?
note: Rationale (noun) = the reasons behind a decision. Rational is the adjective.

text: She has a real _____ for languages and picks them up quickly.
note: A flair for something = a natural talent for it. A flare is a bright light.

text: Candidates are _____ for votes in every village in the district.
note: Canvass = visit people to ask for their support. Canvas is a strong cloth.

text: The cloth was rough and _____ against her skin.
note: Coarse = rough. A course is a series of lessons or the direction of something.

text: A glass of white wine would _____ the meal perfectly.
note: Complement = go well with and improve. Compliment = praise.

text: He told an amusing _____ about his first day at work.
note: An anecdote = a short, amusing true story. An antidote is a medicine against poison.

text: She felt _____ about moving abroad: excited, but also scared.
note: Ambivalent = having mixed feelings. Ambiguous = having more than one possible meaning.

text: She is the _____ of elegance and good taste.
note: The epitome of something = a perfect example of it. An epitaph is words written on a gravestone.

text: She always showed great _____ to her elders.
note: Deference = polite respect for someone. Defiance = open refusal to obey.

text: Your handwriting is _____; I can't read a word of it.
note: Illegible = impossible to read. Legible = easy to read, and eligible = allowed to do something.

text: The smell of fresh bread _____ memories of her grandmother's kitchen.
note: Evoke = bring a memory or feeling into your mind. Invoke = call on a law or a god, and revoke = officially cancel.

text: The disease _____ millions of people every year.
note: Afflict = cause suffering to. Inflict = cause (pain or damage) to someone: it inflicts pain on its victims.

text: The artist mixed her colours on a wooden _____.
note: A palette = a board for mixing paints. The palate is the top of the mouth, and a pallet is a platform for goods.

text: Two years had _____ before she finally returned home.
note: Elapse = (of time) pass. Lapse = stop or fail, especially a membership or a habit.

text: The building has a great _____ appeal, even if it is not practical.
note: Aesthetic = about beauty. An ascetic person lives very simply and avoids pleasure.

text: The entry fee was _____ for students and children.
note: Waive a fee or a rule = choose not to apply it. Wave = move your hand.

text: It was a clever trick, a _____ of hand that fooled everybody.
note: Sleight of hand = skill in using the hands to trick people. Slight means "small".

text: In his speech, the minister _____ to recent financial problems.
note: Allude to = mention indirectly. Elude = escape from. Allege = claim without proof.

text: The poem contains an _____ to a famous Greek myth.
note: Allusion = an indirect reference. Illusion = something that seems real but isn't. Delusion = a false belief.

text: He is an _____ professor of medicine at Oxford University.
note: Eminent = famous and respected. Imminent = about to happen.

text: The course is divided into three _____ units.
note: Discrete = separate and distinct. Discreet = careful about what you say.

text: She was so _____ that she believed every word the salesman said.
note: Ingenuous = innocent and too trusting. Ingenious = clever and inventive.

text: The defendant refused to speak without his _____ present.
note: Counsel = advice, or a lawyer who speaks in court. A council is a governing group; a consul is a diplomat.

text: We need a _____ judge who has no connection with either side.
note: Disinterested = fair, with no personal advantage. Uninterested = not interested, bored.

text: A _____ line of cars stretched along the coast for miles.
note: Continuous = without a break. Continual = repeated again and again (continual interruptions).

text: The law _____ the sale of such weapons to private citizens.
note: Proscribe = forbid officially. Prescribe = order or recommend (a doctor prescribes medicine).

text: In an emergency, safety must take _____ over profit.
note: Take precedence over = be more important than. A precedent is an earlier example that sets a rule.

text: He attacked his dinner with great _____ .
note: Voracity = a huge appetite. Veracity = truthfulness. Vivacity = liveliness.

text: Nobody doubted the _____ of her statement.
note: Veracity = truthfulness. Voracity = a huge appetite.

text: He gave a _____ glance at the cheap furniture.
note: Contemptuous = showing that you think something is worthless. Contemptible = deserving contempt.

text: His _____ enthusiasm for the simplest things was charming.
note: Childlike = having the good qualities of a child (innocent, curious). Childish = silly, like a child, and negative.

text: The judge was _____ to her situation and reduced the sentence.
note: Sympathetic = understanding and kind about someone's problems. It does not mean "nice": for that, use friendly or likeable (Spanish simpático).

text: The instructions were so confusing that they were barely _____ .
note: Comprehensible = possible to understand. Comprehensive = complete, covering everything.

text: He has a guilty _____ about the way he treated her.
note: Conscience = your sense of right and wrong. Conscious = awake and aware. Conscientious = careful and hard-working.

text: She is a very _____ student who always checks her work twice.
note: Conscientious = careful and hard-working. Conscious = aware or awake.

text: The police carried out an _____ search of the area.
note: Exhaustive = very thorough, covering everything. Exhausting = making you very tired.

text: She is determined to _____ at everything she does.
note: Excel at / in something = be very good at it. Exceed = go beyond a limit (exceed the speed limit).

text: It was a very _____ quotation, and the audience nodded in agreement.
note: Apposite = very suitable for the situation. Opposite = completely different or facing.

text: The film's _____ moved the audience to tears.
note: Pathos = a quality that makes you feel pity or sadness. Bathos = a sudden fall from something serious to something silly.

text: She suffers from _____ back pain, which has lasted for years.
note: Chronic = lasting a long time. Acute = sudden and severe.

text: She gave a _____ smile and lowered her eyes.
note: Demure = shy and modest. To demur = to raise an objection.

text: He tried to _____ his true feelings behind a cheerful manner.
note: Dissemble = hide your real feelings or intentions. Disassemble = take something apart.

text: The long afternoon in the heat had _____ him, and he could hardly stand.
note: Enervate = take away strength or energy. (It does not mean "fill with energy".)

text: The _____ on his gravestone reads: "He lived for others".
note: An epitaph = words written on a gravestone. An epithet is a descriptive word added to a name: Alexander the Great.

text: The soldier was _____ in the village churchyard.
note: Inter = bury. Intern = imprison someone without trial.

text: She sued the newspaper for _____ after it published false claims about her.
note: Libel = a false written statement that harms someone's reputation. Slander is the spoken form.

text: I am _____ to leave without saying goodbye.
note: Loath (adjective) = unwilling. Loathe (verb) = hate.

text: The company's _____ display of wealth impressed nobody.
note: Meretricious = attractive in a showy way but without real value. Meritorious = deserving praise.

text: The crisis tested her _____ to the limit.
note: Mettle = courage and strength of character. Metal is a hard material such as iron.

text: The guards patrolled the _____ of the military base.
note: The perimeter = the outer edge of an area. A parameter is a limit or fixed factor.

text: The strange noise _____ her curiosity.
note: Pique = arouse (interest or curiosity). Peak = reach the highest point, and peek = look quickly.

text: A degree is a _____ for the job, so please do not apply without one.
note: A prerequisite = something that must exist first. A perquisite (perk) = an extra benefit that comes with a job.

text: The old buildings were _____ to the ground to make room for a car park.
note: Raze = destroy completely. Raise = lift up.

text: The room _____ of stale cigarette smoke.
note: Reek (of) = smell strongly and unpleasantly. Wreak = cause (havoc, damage).

text: She is a _____ supporter of the local football team and never misses a match.
note: Staunch = very loyal. (Stanch is mostly a verb: to stanch a flow of blood.)

text: The _____ official took bribes from anyone who could pay.
note: Venal = willing to do dishonest things for money. Venial = (of a sin) not very serious.

text: The oil was thick and _____, and it poured very slowly.
note: Viscous = thick and sticky, like honey. Vicious = cruel and violent.

text: He was too _____ to speak up in front of so many people.
note: Diffident = shy and lacking confidence. Indifferent = not interested.

text: Fame is _____: here today, forgotten tomorrow.
note: Ephemeral = lasting for a very short time. Ethereal = very delicate, as if not of this world.

text: After the big lunch she felt _____ and could not stay awake.
note: Lethargic = without energy. Lethal = able to kill.

text: The ship sailed through the _____ of Gibraltar.
note: A strait = a narrow passage of water between two areas of land. Straight means "not curved".

text: It would be _____ of me to speak for the whole team.
note: Presumptuous = behaving with too much confidence, without the right to. Presumptive = based on probability (an heir presumptive).

text: The media often _____ negative stereotypes about young people.
note: Perpetuate = make something continue. Perpetrate = commit a crime or something bad.

text: The couple decided to _____ a child from an orphanage abroad.
note: Adopt = take legally as your own (a child, a policy). Adapt = change to suit a new situation.

text: The hotel's _____ display of wealth put many guests off.
note: Ostentatious = showy, designed to impress. Ostensible = seeming, but perhaps not real.

text: _____, the trip was to discuss trade, but many suspected another purpose.
note: Ostensibly = as it appears, though perhaps not in reality.

text: The waiter was so _____ that it made us feel uncomfortable.
note: Obsequious = too eager to please, in a way that seems false.

text: An _____ little man insisted on checking our tickets twice.
note: Officious = too eager to tell people what to do. Officiate = act as the official in charge of a ceremony or a game.

text: The company's claim was clearly _____ and was quickly rejected.
note: Spurious = false or not genuine. To spurn = to reject with contempt.

text: He gave her a _____ smile, as though he found her question rather silly.
note: Supercilious = behaving as if you are better than other people. Superstitious = believing in luck and magic.

text: Mobile phones are now _____: you see them everywhere.
note: Ubiquitous = seeming to be everywhere. Iniquitous = very unfair or wicked.

text: She felt _____ when the results proved that she had been right all along.
note: Vindicated = shown to be right or innocent. Vindictive = wanting revenge.

text: He is a _____ campaigner who has given his life to the cause.
note: Zealous = full of enthusiasm for a cause. A zealot is the person, and jealous is a different word.

text: The damage to the car was _____ and the insurers paid nothing.
note: Negligible = so small it is not worth considering. Negligent = careless.

text: He was accused of trying to _____ violence among the crowd.
note: Incite = encourage violence or anger. Insight = a deep understanding.

text: The two groups were so _____ that they could find nothing in common.
note: Disparate = completely different from each other. Desperate = in a very bad situation.

text: It was an _____ start to the new season, and the team won easily.
note: Auspicious = showing signs of future success. Suspicious = making you feel something is wrong.

text: The company was accused of using _____ advertising in cinemas.
note: Subliminal = affecting the mind without people being aware of it. Sublime = of very high quality.
